diagram_math_checks.objects: Coordinate slice e2=e3=y1=y2=0 in the R6 chart of Given; u=e1/rho, v=y3/rho^2 with rho>0.
diagram_math_checks.check: Step 1.1 gives y3=e1^2+y1^2+y2^2-rho^2 on the inner cap. Restriction and positive rescaling give exactly v=u^2-1. A has all y coordinates zero, so its slice is v=0. Curves are slices of three-manifolds, explicitly not the entire sheets.

diagram_math_checks.objects: The two intersections q and p.
diagram_math_checks.check: v=0 on the graph implies u=-1 or +1, hence e1=-rho at q and +rho at p as in step 2.1. The rendered graph crosses the horizontal axis at exactly these two marked points. The derivative dv/du=2u is -2 at q and +2 at p.

Step 2.1 uses ordered A basis (d_e1,d_e2,d_e3) and B basis (d_e1+2e1*d_y3,d_y1,d_y2). Relative to Given coordinate order their concatenated determinant is 2e1: subtract the first column from the fourth; moving d_y3 past d_y1,d_y2 is two swaps. Any chosen sheet/ambient orientations multiply both by one common sign. Thus defining epsilon=I(p) makes I(q)=-epsilon, without fixing unstated global orientations.

The horizontal segment q to p lies in A and the graph arc p to q lies in B, with disjoint interiors because u^2-1<0 for -1<u<1. These are embedded arcs meeting only at the two endpoints, giving the local Whitney circle. No orientation arrows or asserted clean framed disk are supplied by the figure. Step 3.1 and F4/F5 supply the cancellation in simply connected S6 with a=b=3=m-3; the figure caption states these hypotheses. The rigorous original verification is unchanged and independent of the figure.
